name: Referral Engine and Viral Coefficient (K-factor) Test
phase: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that our product includes natural referral loops that drive organic growth. We will verify this by adding an in-product referral mechanism to active user workflows, and consider it validated if the measured Viral Coefficient (K) exceeds 0.40: K = i × c where i represents invitations sent per active user, and c represents the conversion rate per invitation.
schematic: Read at step 3 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Put the referral inside the value loop - invite a collaborator to the document - not on a marketing button.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Track invitations, link shares and signups across 300 active users.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Compute the loop variables over time and the cycle time from signup to invited user joining.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Build a frictionless referral touchpoint integrated directly into the core product value loop (e.g., inviting a collaborator to view or edit a document), rather than a generic marketing invite button.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Track invitation generation rates, link shares, and new user signups across 300 active users.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Calculate the viral loop variables over time, tracking the cycle time elapsed between a user signing up and their invited referee joining the platform.

warning.label: Artificial Incentive Distortion
warning.text: Cash rewards buy spam invites that inflate the coefficient and bounce after the payout.

warningFull: Offering high cash or credit rewards can drive high volumes of spam invites, inflating short-term viral numbers with users who bounce immediately after collecting the reward.
